spec.hypothesis: Logistic regression with median imputation, one-hot encoding for the categorical column, and standardization, all fitted inside a pipeline. This mirrors the strong linear baseline while robustly handling missing values and unseen categories.

Improve on the best logistic baseline by using a CatBoost classifier with native categorical/missing handling alongside a regularized logistic model averaged in an ensemble; CatBoost captures nonlinearities while the linear model stabilizes small-data performance. Keep all preprocessing inside the pipeline and use 4 threads with allow_writing_files=False.

The CatBoost repair failed because its ColumnTransformer output remained a numeric/object mixed numpy array with object dtype columns CatBoost could not parse as floats. I will instead keep the best logistic baseline (which scored macro_f1 0.830) and add a small, safe ensemble: a tuned logistic model plus a HistGradientBoosting model on fully numeric one-hot-encoded data, all fitted inside the pipeline. This adds nonlinear capacity without CatBoost's dtype fragility, handles missing values/unseen categories via imputers with handle_unknown, and stays within 4 threads.
